doc.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Pranksters: Billy Eckstine and Dizzy Gillespie
summary: Stories of Eckstine's whoopee cushion for Basie and Dizzy Gillespie's puppet in Perugia, and the curiosity of Basie, Dizzy and Ellington.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Oh, well I guess one thing triggers another thing. But when I first joined Basie’s band, we were just doing little one nighters and so forth. Then we started doing tours with Billy Eckstine and Ruth Brown. Speaking of pranksters, Billy Eckstine was a major prankster. I guess Dizzy was in his band too, I guess that’s where a lot of that stuff came from. We were playing a state-of-the art hall in Richmond, Virginia. And do you know what a whoopy cushion is?

Billy Eckstine put one under the pillow that Basie sat on. So when he sat down — oh, can you imagine that man? You know people would say, because, actually, musicians can become like little — we all have little boys left around in us. We all, Dizzy Gillespie

certainly was one. Boy I guess I’m going through a lot of stories. One brings on another one. Dizzy Gillespie one time we were in Perugia, Italy and about two o’clock in the afternoon, we had come in to the town and we were going out to get some lunch or something. There was a man in the lobby with a puppet on a string. And he was doing nice little things, making the puppet do a lot of stuff. Anyway, Dizzy Gillespie got interested in this thing, so this was about two or three o’clock in the afternoon. And I think he bought it from this guy. So Dizzy Gillespie, with his creative mind, played with the thing the rest of the evening. So about two o’clock in the morning when we were all coming back, we’re sitting around having some wine and stuff, he had that puppet doing everything but talking. It was amazing what a creative mind, because he had that, man he made him jump into your pocket or something. Oh, man, but I always saw that quality about him and Basie and Duke Ellington. They were always curious. What’s this? What’s that? How does that work?
